bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Dependence on customer capital-expenditure cycles — A significant portion of industry revenue depends on large refinery and petrochemical projects. Delays in multi-crore projects can materially impact order inflows and execution schedules, and lower crude oil prices or economic slowdowns may reduce future investments. The MD&A cautionary statement adds that any adverse developments affecting the refinery, petrochemical, fertiliser and chemical industries, or shifts in customer spending patterns, may materially impact the business.
- Raw material price volatility, principally steel — Steel accounts for a major share of equipment manufacturing costs and global steel prices have witnessed fluctuations of over 20-30% during recent years. Sudden increases can pressure margins, particularly under fixed-price contracts. Management lists commodity price fluctuation among its key risks and mitigates it through strategic sourcing, long-term supplier relationships and operational efficiency.
- Project execution risk on long-cycle, customised contracts — The business model involves end-to-end project execution — design, engineering, installation and commissioning — with execution periods often 12-36 months. Complex contracts, stringent timelines and customised requirements increase the risk of delays, cost overruns and quality issues, which can hit customer satisfaction, contractual compliance, execution costs and working capital. Mitigated through a Risk Management Policy and framework, internal and external audits and stage-wise quality assurance protocols.
- Supply chain concentration and disruption — Supply chain disruptions affect the availability of raw materials and finished goods, and dependence on specific suppliers or regions exposes the Company to geopolitical, market and logistical risks that can delay production and delivery. Mitigation is prospective: the Company intends to maintain adequate supplier inventories, develop alternative domestic sourcing models and adopt digital tools for supply-chain visibility.
- Intense competition in a competitively bid market — The industry competes with established domestic and international engineering companies, and large projects are typically awarded through competitive bidding. Aggressive pricing can reduce margins despite healthy market demand.
- Single-activity and single-sector concentration — A structural concentration disclosed in the BRSR rather than labelled a risk: 100.00% of FY 2026 turnover comes from one activity — engineering services for industrial and manufacturing projects (NIC 42909), the design, manufacture and installation of process-fired heaters, reformers and cracking furnaces — serving customers concentrated in oil and gas, refining, petrochemical, fertiliser and chemical manufacturing. Exports contributed 12.45% of total turnover. These BRSR figures appear in the registry bundle of this same annual report rather than in the risks routing.
- Skilled-labour availability and workforce attrition — Limited availability of skilled labour can affect the ability to meet project timelines, budget requirements and quality standards, creating workforce management and communication challenges and increasing the likelihood of errors and safety incidents. The BRSR (carried in the registry bundle of the same annual report) shows FY 2026 turnover rates of 21.7% for permanent employees and 70.4% for permanent workers, sharply up from 7.74% and 9.30% in FY 2025. The Company plans to establish a labour management system and introduce digital tools.
- Occupational health and safety exposure across sites and contractors — Safety lapses can cause workplace incidents, operational disruption and broader business implications, with financial consequences spanning medical expenses, compensation payouts, project delays, regulatory penalties and reputational risk. The Company operates an ISO 45001:2018 management system, a comprehensive HSE Policy, quarterly HSE audits, dedicated site HSE managers and safety training, and its HSE system now covers offices, fabrication facilities, warehouses and construction sites and extends to contractors and partners.
- Climate change and tightening environmental regulation — Extreme weather events such as heatwaves, heavy rainfall and storms can disrupt project schedules, increase costs and affect workforce safety, while evolving environmental regulation and rising ESG expectations may cause asset obsolescence and reduced market demand. Mitigated by an Environmental Management Plan aligned to ISO 14001:2015, a 50 kWp solar plant at the manufacturing facility and a plan to maintain project-specific climate risk profiles.
- Cyber security and data protection gap — The BRSR states that in the absence of cybersecurity measures the Company faces risks of data breaches compromising employee information and exposing confidential client and financial data and critical business assets such as project plans and bid strategies. The mitigating cyber security policy and framework is still being developed and implemented.

outlook.body: The Company strengthened its manufacturing backbone during FY 2026 through a significant upgrade of its Mundra, Gujarat facility, creating an integrated, modern platform for end-to-end manufacturing of critical process heater components; management states the enhanced capabilities improve capacity, productivity, quality and safety, enable faster execution and position the Company to undertake larger and more complex projects as it scales. The Mundra site sits in a multi-product SEZ suited to export-oriented fabrication and modularisation, benefits from proximity to a deep-draft port for ODC cargo handling, is spread over 20,243 square metres and carries an installed fabrication capacity of 5,000 MT. Capability expansion during the year was primarily inorganic and partnership-led rather than brownfield: on August 20, 2025 the Company incorporated the joint venture JNK Chemdist Technologies Private Limited (JNK India 51%, Chemdist 49%) with Mr. Tushar Wagh, Dr. Sunil Dhole and another investor, to research, develop, market, engineer, manufacture and supply green hydrogen and other technologies; its stated focus areas are scaling ethanol-to-chemicals and low-opex hydrogen production towards commercialisation, delivering turnkey solutions for the chemical, pharmaceutical and process industries, and deploying advanced membrane technologies. The Company also operates two wholly owned subsidiaries — JNK India Private FZE, engaged in erection works of CCR, NHT, MHC and CDU (A, B and C) Heaters for the Dangote Oil Refinery and petrochemicals project, and JNK Renewable Energy Private Limited in Solar EPC. On the energy side, a 50 kWp solar power plant has been installed at the manufacturing facility, and the Company plans to establish and maintain project-specific climate risk profiles where required. Looking ahead, management intends to deepen presence in established markets, expand the product and service portfolio, pursue carefully selected adjacent opportunities and selectively increase international presence across the Middle East, Africa and Southeast Asia, alongside technology-led diversification into process plants, green energy solutions, metals and mining and offshore. BRSR Section A records one operational location and seven offices in India and no international operational locations or offices. outlook.body:
- Demand from the refining, petrochemical, fertiliser and energy sectors remains strong, and management states JNK India remains well-positioned for growth on the back of it
- Growth in refining and petrochemical capex: India's refining capacity exceeds 250 MMTPA with multiple expansion projects under implementation, and the petrochemical sector is expected to grow at 7-8% CAGR over the medium term, expected to drive demand for process-fired heaters, reformers and thermal equipment
- Energy transition and green hydrogen: India targets 5 MMT of green hydrogen production annually by 2030 under the National Green Hydrogen Mission, with industrial decarbonisation and sustainable fuel projects attracting significant investment, creating opportunities for advanced process and heating technologies
- Stricter environmental regulations: industries are investing in low-emission combustion systems and energy-efficient equipment, with India aiming to cut the emissions intensity of GDP by 45% from 2005 levels by 2030, increasing demand for emission-control and energy-efficiency solutions
- Modularisation and offsite fabrication: modular construction can reduce project schedules by 20-50% versus conventional methods, and owners increasingly adopt offsite fabrication, supporting demand for integrated engineering and project execution capability
- Indian government capital expenditure of over Rs 11.2 lakh crore is expected to support transportation, energy, logistics and industrial infrastructure, while investment in refining and petrochemicals sustains demand for process equipment and engineering solutions
- Increasing investments in energy efficiency, decarbonisation and clean energy solutions place the Company to capitalise on emerging opportunities
- Countervailing threats management flags: dependence on capital-expenditure cycles, raw material (steel) price volatility under fixed-price contracts, intense competitive bidding, and project execution and supply chain risk on 12-36 month project cycles
- Management enters FY 2027 with a stronger platform, a healthy order book, enhanced execution capabilities and a broader opportunity landscape
- Order inflows of Rs 1,694.4 crore during FY 2026, described as the largest-ever order inflow, an 81.2% YoY growth
- Order book of Rs 1,961.4 crore as of March 31, 2026, an all-time high, providing meaningful revenue visibility and a strong foundation for the years ahead
- The award of a critical large cracking furnace order, bagged by partner and promoter JNK Global, drove the record inflow
- Work orders were booked from JNK Global Co. Ltd., Korea on August 22, 2025, October 6, 2025 and March 27, 2026 for design and engineering support for the Cracker Furnace Package of a refinery project in India
- Critical projects secured in cracking furnaces and green hydrogen, alongside diversification into technology-based process plants, waste gas handling systems and specialised process equipment
- Robust order book cited as a value driver providing strong revenue visibility
- Order-book milestones in the company timeline: past Rs 500 crore in 2022 after a major export order in Mexico, and above Rs 1,800 crore in 2025 alongside the Chemdist JV
- Order inflows were subdued at the start of FY 2026 with the first quarter considerably below expectations, before performance strengthened progressively from the second quarter

risks.note: A significant portion of industry revenue depends on large refinery and petrochemical projects. Delays in multi-crore projects can materially impact order inflows and execution schedules, and lower crude oil prices or economic slowdowns may reduce future investments. The MD&A cautionary statement adds that any adverse developments affecting the refinery, petrochemical, fertiliser and chemical industries, or shifts in customer spending patterns, may materially impact the business.

risks.risk: Raw material price volatility, principally steel
risks.note: Steel accounts for a major share of equipment manufacturing costs and global steel prices have witnessed fluctuations of over 20-30% during recent years. Sudden increases can pressure margins, particularly under fixed-price contracts. Management lists commodity price fluctuation among its key risks and mitigates it through strategic sourcing, long-term supplier relationships and operational efficiency.

risks.risk: Project execution risk on long-cycle, customised contracts
risks.note: The business model involves end-to-end project execution — design, engineering, installation and commissioning — with execution periods often 12-36 months. Complex contracts, stringent timelines and customised requirements increase the risk of delays, cost overruns and quality issues, which can hit customer satisfaction, contractual compliance, execution costs and working capital. Mitigated through a Risk Management Policy and framework, internal and external audits and stage-wise quality assurance protocols.

Supply chain disruptions affect the availability of raw materials and finished goods, and dependence on specific suppliers or regions exposes the Company to geopolitical, market and logistical risks that can delay production and delivery. Mitigation is prospective: the Company intends to maintain adequate supplier inventories, develop alternative domestic sourcing models and adopt digital tools for supply-chain visibility.

risks.risk: Intense competition in a competitively bid market
risks.note: The industry competes with established domestic and international engineering companies, and large projects are typically awarded through competitive bidding. Aggressive pricing can reduce margins despite healthy market demand.

A structural concentration disclosed in the BRSR rather than labelled a risk: 100.00% of FY 2026 turnover comes from one activity — engineering services for industrial and manufacturing projects (NIC 42909), the design, manufacture and installation of process-fired heaters, reformers and cracking furnaces — serving customers concentrated in oil and gas, refining, petrochemical, fertiliser and chemical manufacturing. Exports contributed 12.45% of total turnover. These BRSR figures appear in the registry bundle of this same annual report rather than in the risks routing.

Limited availability of skilled labour can affect the ability to meet project timelines, budget requirements and quality standards, creating workforce management and communication challenges and increasing the likelihood of errors and safety incidents. The BRSR (carried in the registry bundle of the same annual report) shows FY 2026 turnover rates of 21.7% for permanent employees and 70.4% for permanent workers, sharply up from 7.74% and 9.30% in FY 2025. The Company plans to establish a labour management system and introduce digital tools.

risks.risk: Occupational health and safety exposure across sites and contractors
risks.note: Safety lapses can cause workplace incidents, operational disruption and broader business implications, with financial consequences spanning medical expenses, compensation payouts, project delays, regulatory penalties and reputational risk. The Company operates an ISO 45001:2018 management system, a comprehensive HSE Policy, quarterly HSE audits, dedicated site HSE managers and safety training, and its HSE system now covers offices, fabrication facilities, warehouses and construction sites and extends to contractors and partners.

risks.risk: Climate change and tightening environmental regulation
risks.note: Extreme weather events such as heatwaves, heavy rainfall and storms can disrupt project schedules, increase costs and affect workforce safety, while evolving environmental regulation and rising ESG expectations may cause asset obsolescence and reduced market demand. Mitigated by an Environmental Management Plan aligned to ISO 14001:2015, a 50 kWp solar plant at the manufacturing facility and a plan to maintain project-specific climate risk profiles.

risks.risk: Cyber security and data protection gap
risks.note: The BRSR states that in the absence of cybersecurity measures the Company faces risks of data breaches compromising employee information and exposing confidential client and financial data and critical business assets such as project plans and bid strategies. The mitigating cyber security policy and framework is still being developed and implemented.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Demand from the refining, petrochemical, fertiliser and energy sectors remains strong, and management states JNK India remains well-positioned for growth on the back of it
- Growth in refining and petrochemical capex: India's refining capacity exceeds 250 MMTPA with multiple expansion projects under implementation, and the petrochemical sector is expected to grow at 7-8% CAGR over the medium term, expected to drive demand for process-fired heaters, reformers and thermal equipment
- Energy transition and green hydrogen: India targets 5 MMT of green hydrogen production annually by 2030 under the National Green Hydrogen Mission, with industrial decarbonisation and sustainable fuel projects attracting significant investment, creating opportunities for advanced process and heating technologies
- Stricter environmental regulations: industries are investing in low-emission combustion systems and energy-efficient equipment, with India aiming to cut the emissions intensity of GDP by 45% from 2005 levels by 2030, increasing demand for emission-control and energy-efficiency solutions
- Modularisation and offsite fabrication: modular construction can reduce project schedules by 20-50% versus conventional methods, and owners increasingly adopt offsite fabrication, supporting demand for integrated engineering and project execution capability
- Indian government capital expenditure of over Rs 11.2 lakh crore is expected to support transportation, energy, logistics and industrial infrastructure, while investment in refining and petrochemicals sustains demand for process equipment and engineering solutions
- Increasing investments in energy efficiency, decarbonisation and clean energy solutions place the Company to capitalise on emerging opportunities
- Countervailing threats management flags: dependence on capital-expenditure cycles, raw material (steel) price volatility under fixed-price contracts, intense competitive bidding, and project execution and supply chain risk on 12-36 month project cycles
- Management enters FY 2027 with a stronger platform, a healthy order book, enhanced execution capabilities and a broader opportunity landscape
- Order inflows of Rs 1,694.4 crore during FY 2026, described as the largest-ever order inflow, an 81.2% YoY growth
- Order book of Rs 1,961.4 crore as of March 31, 2026, an all-time high, providing meaningful revenue visibility and a strong foundation for the years ahead
- The award of a critical large cracking furnace order, bagged by partner and promoter JNK Global, drove the record inflow
- Work orders were booked from JNK Global Co. Ltd., Korea on August 22, 2025, October 6, 2025 and March 27, 2026 for design and engineering support for the Cracker Furnace Package of a refinery project in India
- Critical projects secured in cracking furnaces and green hydrogen, alongside diversification into technology-based process plants, waste gas handling systems and specialised process equipment
- Robust order book cited as a value driver providing strong revenue visibility
- Order-book milestones in the company timeline: past Rs 500 crore in 2022 after a major export order in Mexico, and above Rs 1,800 crore in 2025 alongside the Chemdist JV
- Order inflows were subdued at the start of FY 2026 with the first quarter considerably below expectations, before performance strengthened progressively from the second quarter

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company strengthened its manufacturing backbone during FY 2026 through a significant upgrade of its Mundra, Gujarat facility, creating an integrated, modern platform for end-to-end manufacturing of critical process heater components; management states the enhanced capabilities improve capacity, productivity, quality and safety, enable faster execution and position the Company to undertake larger and more complex projects as it scales. The Mundra site sits in a multi-product SEZ suited to export-oriented fabrication and modularisation, benefits from proximity to a deep-draft port for ODC cargo handling, is spread over 20,243 square metres and carries an installed fabrication capacity of 5,000 MT. Capability expansion during the year was primarily inorganic and partnership-led rather than brownfield: on August 20, 2025 the Company incorporated the joint venture JNK Chemdist Technologies Private Limited (JNK India 51%, Chemdist 49%) with Mr. Tushar Wagh, Dr. Sunil Dhole and another investor, to research, develop, market, engineer, manufacture and supply green hydrogen and other technologies; its stated focus areas are scaling ethanol-to-chemicals and low-opex hydrogen production towards commercialisation, delivering turnkey solutions for the chemical, pharmaceutical and process industries, and deploying advanced membrane technologies. The Company also operates two wholly owned subsidiaries — JNK India Private FZE, engaged in erection works of CCR, NHT, MHC and CDU (A, B and C) Heaters for the Dangote Oil Refinery and petrochemicals project, and JNK Renewable Energy Private Limited in Solar EPC. On the energy side, a 50 kWp solar power plant has been installed at the manufacturing facility, and the Company plans to establish and maintain project-specific climate risk profiles where required. Looking ahead, management intends to deepen presence in established markets, expand the product and service portfolio, pursue carefully selected adjacent opportunities and selectively increase international presence across the Middle East, Africa and Southeast Asia, alongside technology-led diversification into process plants, green energy solutions, metals and mining and offshore. BRSR Section A records one operational location and seven offices in India and no international operational locations or offices. No rupee capex quantum is usable from this bundle: the two capital-commitment blocks supplied carry no printed unit, and the segment capital-expenditure block carries no figure.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Long-standing working relationship with JNK Global, a KOSDAQ-listed company that is also a promoter and technology partner; this partnership opened new geographies and strengthens the ability to secure complex, critical and larger ticket-sized orders through its brand legacy
- Deep customer relationships supported by a proven record of developing and delivering customised solutions
- Concept-to-commissioning model providing end-to-end project execution through a single point of contact, often structured as a License plus EPCC arrangement
- Technology-agnostic approach — not tied to any single technology provider, allowing selection of the technology best suited to each project
- Successfully overcame high entry barriers in a specialised industry
- Robust order book providing strong revenue visibility
- In-house thermal design and specialised engineering expertise, described as the heart of its competitive advantage, with a workforce of over 450 employees across design, execution and R&D
- Upgraded, integrated Mundra manufacturing backbone in a multi-product SEZ near a deep-draft port, improving capacity, productivity, quality and safety and enabling larger, more complex projects

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Execution timing slippage (Reliance spilling to Q1 FY27); Dangote order finalization uncertainty (expected Q3 FY27); CBG technology/feedstock stabilization issues limiting domestic uptake; Dependency on large lump-sum orders causing quarterly volatility; Labor code compliance costs.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Accounting policy shift (output to input method) is the primary driver of margin normalization, not operating leverage or pricing; Mundra facility utilization is low not due to demand but lack of specific export projects under execution; JV revenue (Rs 23 Cr) already flowing in first quarter of operation, faster than typical R&D spin-offs; Bank guarantee structure via JNK Global significantly de-risks balance sheet for large tenders.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Order cancellation] The large export order received on June 8, 2026 was cancelled solely due to inability to secure the requisite technical approval from the licensor; the deck states this was an isolated incident, with no material costs incurred and no execution having commenced.
- [JV structure] The Chemdist joint venture is held JNK India 51% / Chemdist Technology 49%, with Chemdist contributing proprietary technologies and IP, advanced R&D and process innovation, and JNK contributing EPC execution, manufacturing and global project execution.
- [New consolidation] The deck repeatedly footnotes that Q1FY27 Total Income includes Revenue of Rs 16.5 cr from JNK Chemdist Limited, which was not part of Q1FY26 — i.e. the YoY comparison is not like-for-like.
- [Restatement] The deck states financial information for previous periods has been regrouped/reclassified to conform to appropriate presentation and comparability, wherever necessary.
- [Board] Board includes Arvind Kamath (Chairperson & WTD), Goutam Rampelli (Vice Chairperson & WTD), Dipak Bharuka (CEO & WTD) and Bang Hee Kim (Non-Executive Director, formerly DL E&C CO and adjunct professor at Yonsei University), reflecting the Korean partnership at board level.
